reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/mark.rs owns static mark/file_mark arrays; each record borrows an IFILE handle and can separately own a saved filename. cmarkf first retires previous record filename state, then saves a new filename copy.
owner_creation.invariant: Static mark storage and allocated filename fields have different ownership.
limitations: Neither array owns the underlying input file bytes or descriptor.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/mark.rs returns interior mark pointers and retains raw IFILE addresses with copied screen positions. mark_get_ifile converts a retained filename into a selected raw handle and releases the stored filename.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A raw file handle requires current-file/list lifetime validation.
limitations: The copied POSITION has no file-generation token.

callback_targets.analysis: src/mark.rs setmark directly asks position/line services for coordinates and may call save_cmdhist after publishing the mark. These calls cross owners without a retained callback context.
callback_targets.invariant: Position lookup and history save must preserve the selected record contract.
limitations: Ordinary direct calls do not provide a Rust exclusive borrow of the mark array.

invalidation.analysis: src/mark.rs unmark invalidates matching mark positions and last-search position but does not free the static record or replace it with a typed retired handle. File association changes separately free saved names.
invalidation.invariant: Logical mark invalidation must precede reuse of its stale file identity.
limitations: An address-valid static record can still represent an invalid position.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/mark.rs cmark assigns IFILE and screen coordinates before freeing/nulling a previous filename; setmark later sets marks_modified and may autosave. These are separate shared-state writes.
mutation_commit.invariant: File identity, position and persistence state require a coherent completed mark.
limitations: No staged aggregate guarantees rollback across a later history-save call.

release_pair.analysis: src/mark.rs cmark frees only the previous saved filename, and mark_check_ifile frees its temporary canonical path after matching. The image arrays and borrowed IFILE must never take that free counterpart.
release_pair.invariant: Only saved or canonicalized filename allocations are allocator-owned here.
limitations: Mark invalidation alone neither closes the file nor frees a mark array element.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/mark.rs malformed restored mark text returns before cmarkf publication, while failed position lookup reports and leaves the selected mark unmodified. Fatal save allocation has no local rollback Result.
error_cleanup.invariant: Input validation must precede replacing a stored mark owner.
limitations: No fresh persistent-mark parser campaign accompanies this source review.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/mark.rs mutates ordinary static records and a global dirty flag without an encoded handler-exclusion or file-generation protocol. M0-MEM-001 stays open for that shared raw owner coordination.
signals_handoff.invariant: Mark operations require serialized access to stable file/navigation state.
limitations: No specific handler-to-mark mutation route is established in this file.
